story: Yudhishthira, eldest Pandava and son of Yama, the god of dharma, was famous for never telling a lie. Yet he gambled away his kingdom, his brothers, himself and finally Draupadi in a rigged dice game, sending the family into 13 years of exile.
belief: He is called Dharmaraja, the king of righteousness. He answered the Yaksha's riddles at the lake to bring his brothers back to life, and he is the only one in the Mahabharata who reaches heaven in his own body.
turns: Gambling was his weakness, and he could not refuse a challenge. In the war he announced 'Ashwatthama is dead', meaning an elephant and muttering the last part, so that Drona would put down his weapons.
facts: His chariot was said to float above the ground until he told that half-truth.
He refused to enter heaven without the dog that had followed him.
The Yaksha Prashna, his dialogue of riddles, is one of the most quoted parts of the Mahabharata.
